research_question: Can source-neutral, FIT-learned sparse Boolean cross-bit operators discover nonbitwise causal arithmetic relationships from 24 eight-event sequences, and can a compact bit-parallel compiler match full CPU cost of an independently optimized equally trained polynomial peer? Do not supply ADD/carry/rotate function templates to learners.
source_only_authoring: Fresh internally authored separate source-only deterministic task families, no original scientific 924-937, no F124-DD 81-84 case replay, seeds frozen before new source code. Source labels hidden from model.
shared_hypothesis: Unlabeled source-neutral mapping of TWO unknown public 4-bit registers (8 raw input bits) to an arbitrary learned 4-bit output. Generic full degree<=4 Boolean polynomial in those 8 bits (163 monomials per output). Model scans all ten input-register pairs and learns four output-bit coefficient vectors, source law and operator family NOT supplied. Higher degree and three-register laws are deliberately out of scope. This is a PROVIDED BOUNDED mathematical vocabulary, not unrestricted operator invention.

All no-fit and no-CHECK abstentions retained. No heldout or CHECK tuning.
